properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-20, thinking past both hypotheticals: *"I feel like we could do this and set a far off target epoch for reflow2, then the question becomes how to change/morph reflow2 to that future state."*

DISTINCT FROM BOTH SIBLINGS, which were read before writing this. `dec:idea-genesis-reflow3-from-the-requirements-alone` asks what a fresh pass on the requirements would PRODUCE — a sufficiency test. `dec:idea-run-adopt-on-reflow2-itself-as-a-ground-truth-test` asks what reading the CODE would RECOVER. Both are EXPERIMENTS that end in a measurement. This is a MECHANISM that ends in a roadmap, and it needs neither experiment to be run.

⭐ THE MACHINERY IS ALREADY BUILT, which is what makes this cheap where reflow3 is expensive:
  `plan_epoch`      an Epoch that has NOT happened yet — the forward half of the time axis
                    (`req:epochs-can-be-planned`). A planned epoch REFUSES record_change,
                    because a snapshot captures the present.
  `schedule_for`    points a Requirement or Capability at the epoch it is due in
  `arrival_delta`   planned versus delivered, per item, with FIVE outcomes — delivered,
                    deferred, discontinued, and `outstanding`, which means nobody has yet
                    said which of the previous two it is. It refuses to default that, and
                    names it as the question to put to the user.
  `set_epoch_status` marks arrival when the moment comes

⇒ SO "HOW DO WE MORPH REFLOW2 TO ITS FUTURE STATE" IS ALREADY A COMPUTABLE QUESTION. Record the end state as a planned epoch, schedule the intent that belongs to it, and the delta between now and then IS the roadmap — recomputed on demand rather than maintained as a document that drifts.

⭐⭐ AND IT DISSOLVES THE EXPENSIVE HALF OF THE REFLOW3 QUESTION. reflow3 was proposed to discover whether the recorded intent determines the product. But the reason a fresh pass would diverge is already measured and is not in doubt: 18 capabilities no requirement asks for, 43 requirements nothing delivers, and a design governed more than twice as heavily by Decisions (877 of 901 GOVERNED_BY edges) as by Requirements — and genesis does not take Decisions as input. A target epoch does not need to answer that question. It needs the target STATED, which is a thing Anthony can say directly.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⚠️ WHAT IS GENUINELY HARD ABOUT IT, and it is not the tooling

A planned epoch is only as good as the target written into it, and NOBODY HAS WRITTEN ONE. Today's audit gives candidate content — every 15288 process with vocabulary and no check, the interface half of the black-box requirement, a risk register, validation that has never once been used on 175 checks. But turning that into a stated end-state is a design act, not a scheduling one.

🛑 AND ONE TRAP THIS SHARES WITH EVERYTHING ELSE TODAY: `arrival_delta` computes against the epoch's FIRST snapshot as baseline. A target epoch with nothing scheduled at it returns a clean delta — the same green-over-emptiness shape as `modularity 1.00` over one dependency, `hierarchy_issues: 0` over an incomplete spine, and `0 gaps` over ten unused schema domains. A far-off epoch nobody has scheduled anything into would report no shortfall at all.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
OPTIONS

**A. STATE THE TARGET, SCHEDULE NOTHING YET.** One planned epoch, named, with the end-state written in its own text. Cheapest possible move and it makes the direction a fact rather than a conversation. ⚠️ On its own it changes no computation.

**B. STATE IT AND SCHEDULE THE KNOWN GAPS INTO IT** — the accepted-but-unbuilt requirements, starting with `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` and `req:interface-spec-complete`. `arrival_delta` then answers "how far is reflow2 from what it says it should be" as a computation. ⭐ This is the one that makes the morph measurable.

**C. INTERMEDIATE EPOCHS BETWEEN NOW AND THE TARGET** — the increments. `plan-increments` already exists for this. ⚠️ Premature until the target has content; sequencing toward an unstated end is how a roadmap becomes a wish list.

**D. DO IT AFTER ADOPT.** Anthony's own leaning is adopt-on-a-copy first. Its predicted prize is a RECOVERED CONTRACT SET, which is precisely the largest item any target epoch would contain — so running it first would populate the target rather than guess at it.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a planned epoch far enough out to hold a whole end-state is a shape reflow2 has ever exercised. Every epoch in this graph is a release cut or a revision that has already happened.
properties.name: OPEN — record reflow2's target end-state as a PLANNED EPOCH and let arrival_delta drive the morph, instead of building reflow3 to find out what the target is
